text:
lena: Heads up — seeing a weird canary failure on fncall validation: runtime rejects tool response then runtime routes to fallback and it still counts against quota. anyone else?

mike: saw a blip like that in beta. did the logs show a timeout vs schema mismatch?

lena: paste from logs:
```
deploy-bot: canary deploy started by jess at 2026-03-19T17:02:00Z
INVOKE: route=/checkout fn=order_service
TOOL_RESPONSE: { "order_id": 4321, "items": null }
VALIDATOR: validate_fncall(order_service) FAILED -> error: "Expected array for items but got null"
ROUTER: fallback -> model=small-gpt-2 (policy=permissive-fallback)
BILLING: tokens charged, metric=fncall_reject_count++
```

karim: that looks like strict_validate=true for the canary slice. if the validator errors we currently classify as a single "fncall_reject" metric which loses the reason.

sophia: +1 to splitting it out. proposal: expose fncall.validation_outcome with tags: outcome=(ok|soft_coerce|hard_reject|timeout) and reason=(type_mismatch|missing_field|too_long|other) and adapter=order_service.

jess: console UX: we should show a tiny diff view in the per-route dashboard for canaries (example payload vs validated shape) and a "grace period" toggle so teams can opt into automatic coercion during rollout. also quota semantics: soft_coerce should not count as a hard reject for rollback triggers.

mike: implementation idea: add a counter metric fncall.validation_level{level=strict|permissive|coerce} and an enumerated fncall.validation_outcome tag. export a 1% sampled JSON blob to S3 with the raw tool response + validated coercions for audit.

ops-bot: alert suggestion: create alert when fncall.validation_outcome=hard_reject rate > 0.5% for 5m on prod routes.

karim: question: what do we actually coerce? null->[]? string->number? we should constrain coercion per-adapter (order_service can coerce null->[] for items but payment_service cannot). avoid surprising silent changes.

lena: thinking we do a short grace: for new canaries set validation_mode=permissive_coerce for 48h, collect diffs + counts, highlight in console, then require explicit opt-in to flip strict_validate on. that buys customers time to fix producers without outages.

jess: I'll spin up a tiny RFC + console mock this afternoon. owners: @karim to design coercion rules per adapter, @mike to add telemetry tags + sampling, @lena to run the canary and collect examples.

mike: assigning now. i'll also add a flag to the runtime so deploy-bot can pause strict rollouts.

deploy-bot: Canary paused for 6h per request from mike.

lena: thanks. one more: make sure billing/usage dashboards clearly separate soft_coerce events so SRE and billing talk to customers with the same story.

sophia: agree — add an explicit cost_tag for coerced_vs_reject so finance can filter.

mike: will do. i'll post a follow-up PR with metrics names and a small sampling payload example.

jess: :thumbsup: will track RFC and mock in the rollout board.

lena: cool — tagging this as follow-up for the validation/rollout epic.

ops-bot: created ticket FNVALID-482 and linked to epic VALIDATION-EPIC.

mike: quick note — avoid changing default behavior for existing prod routes; opt-in only. we don't want surprise regressions.

karim: agreed. coercion profiles per-adapter + opt-in per-route. i'll draft rules and corner cases.

lena: awesome, thanks everyone.
